answer: Three nights a week watchers climb the ridge and log every meteor before dawn, and the roster names the watcher for each night of the season. A oasis sighting invented at breakfast fails the roster: at the onyx of the sky the meteor must have fallen where the watcher wrote, and an invented one falls nowhere. To fake the roster a forger must post watchers for a whole season, log 180 nights and pay 9,400, and the bridge entry in the watch book is read by the station chief each morning, so a meteor that was never seen earns no mark.
